name: Password Security Checkup
summary: Review password habits, shared account risks, and password manager readiness.
marketingHeadline: Password Security Checkup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Weak, reused, or previously leaked passwords are the single most common way small businesses get breached. The Password Security Checkup gives you a practical audit of how your company actually handles credentials today. We review your Microsoft 365 password policies, scan your business email domain against the HaveIBeenPwned breach database to see which accounts have been exposed, document shared logins and generic mailboxes that create accountability gaps, and assess whether a business password manager like Bitwarden, 1Password, or Keeper is the right fit. You receive a plain-English scorecard and a prioritized list of fixes you can act on immediately, plus a 30-minute walkthrough so you fully understand what we found and what to do next.
bestFor: Businesses that reuse the same password across multiple accounts or systems
Companies where staff share login credentials through spreadsheets or chat
Organizations that have never reviewed their password policies or breached-account exposure
Businesses applying for cyber insurance that need evidence of password hygiene
whatIsIncluded: Full password policy audit across Microsoft 365 and known cloud platforms
Domain-wide compromised-credential scan using the HaveIBeenPwned API
Shared account and generic mailbox inventory with risk assessment
Password manager readiness evaluation comparing Bitwarden, 1Password, and Keeper
Plain-English Password Security Scorecard with prioritized recommendations
30-minute customer walkthrough of findings and next steps
customerOutcomes: A clear, documented picture of your password posture across every business system
Knowledge of exactly which business accounts have been exposed in known breaches
A prioritized, low-effort plan for eliminating weak, shared, and reused credentials
Credible password hygiene evidence you can submit with cyber insurance applications

name: MFA Setup Session
summary: Configure or guide multi-factor authentication for critical business accounts.
marketingHeadline: MFA Setup Session from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Multi-factor authentication stops more than 99% of automated account-takeover attacks, yet most small businesses still rely on a password alone for email, banking, payroll, and cloud apps. The MFA Setup Session audits every critical business account for MFA coverage, then configures it hands-on where you have admin access. We enforce MFA with a Microsoft 365 Conditional Access policy so it applies to every user automatically, enable Google Workspace 2-Step Verification when applicable, and walk you through securing third-party platforms like your domain registrar, payroll provider, and banking portals. Every user gets clear enrollment instructions, we verify sign-in works across phone and desktop apps, and we document recovery codes safely so nobody gets permanently locked out.
bestFor: Businesses that don't have MFA enabled on email, banking, payroll, or cloud accounts
Organizations whose cyber insurance now requires MFA across all critical accounts
Companies that need hands-on help enabling MFA without confusing technical documentation
Businesses that recently suffered an email or account compromise and want it to stop happening
whatIsIncluded: Audit of all business-critical accounts to identify MFA gaps
Microsoft 365 MFA configuration with a Conditional Access policy that applies to every user
Google Workspace 2-Step Verification setup when applicable
Guided MFA enablement for third-party platforms (banking, payroll, CRM, domain registrar)
Authenticator app enrollment and training for all users with recovery code storage
Post-configuration sign-in testing on every platform we secure
customerOutcomes: MFA enforced on email, cloud apps, and every critical third-party account we can reach
A Conditional Access policy in Microsoft 365 that blocks sign-ins without a second factor
Staff enrolled and comfortable using an authenticator app with no lockouts or confusion
Documented MFA status per platform that satisfies insurance and audit requests

name: Phishing Readiness Mini Audit
summary: Review basic email scam readiness and staff handling practices.
marketingHeadline: Phishing Readiness Mini Audit from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Phishing is the attack path behind most real-world business breaches, and the question every owner asks is: would my staff actually recognize it? The Phishing Readiness Mini Audit gives you a fast, evidence-based answer. We review your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records so we know whether someone can spoof your domain, audit your Microsoft 365 anti-phishing and anti-spam settings, scan user mailboxes for suspicious forwarding rules that indicate a takeover, and optionally run a safe, controlled phishing simulation to measure real click and report rates. You get a clear scorecard of your email defenses and your team's awareness, with specific fixes ranked by impact.
bestFor: Businesses that receive phishing emails and want to know whether staff would fall for them
Organizations that have never reviewed their email authentication or anti-phishing settings
Companies preparing for cyber insurance that asks about phishing awareness testing
Businesses that experienced a phishing-related compromise or near-miss and want a baseline
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC record audit to detect spoofable email domains
Microsoft 365 anti-phishing policy review including impersonation protection
Microsoft 365 anti-spam and quarantine settings review
Mailbox forwarding-rule audit to spot signs of account compromise
Optional controlled phishing simulation with click, report, and reply metrics
Phishing Readiness Scorecard with prioritized remediation steps
customerOutcomes: A clear picture of whether your email domain can be impersonated and how to stop it
Measured staff phishing awareness compared against realistic expectations
Specific Microsoft 365 settings changes that meaningfully reduce phishing risk
An actionable scorecard you can reuse to track awareness improvements over time

name: Security Score Snapshot
summary: Create a lightweight cyber posture snapshot covering identity, endpoint, backup, email, and admin risk.
marketingHeadline: Security Score Snapshot from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Most small businesses have never had a formal security assessment, so they guess where the risk is instead of knowing. The Security Score Snapshot replaces guesswork with a single number you can track. We evaluate five domains that matter most for a small organization - identity, endpoints, email, backup, and admin access - against practical baseline controls, then score you 0 to 100. Each domain gets a red, amber, or green rating with the specific evidence behind it, and we finish with your top five quick-win fixes ranked by risk reduction versus effort. This is a fast, affordable baseline you can rerun quarterly to prove you're improving, and it produces exactly the kind of evidence cyber insurers want to see.
bestFor: Business owners who want an objective, measurable security score rather than gut feeling
Organizations that have never had any security assessment and need a starting baseline
Companies applying for cyber insurance that need a gap list and improvement evidence
Businesses that want to measure security improvement over time with a repeatable score
whatIsIncluded: Identity review: MFA coverage, admin accounts, and shared credential risk
Endpoint review: protection software, patch status, encryption, and local admin rights
Email review: SPF/DKIM/DMARC, anti-phishing policy, and mailbox-rule risk
Backup review: configuration, success history, retention, and off-site copy
Admin access review: privileged accounts, stale accounts, and excessive permissions
Security Scorecard with an overall 0-100 score and five prioritized quick wins

name: Admin Account Cleanup
summary: Identify unnecessary admin rights, stale admin accounts, and shared privileged logins.
marketingHeadline: Admin Account Cleanup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Every former employee, past IT provider, and abandoned project usually leaves behind an admin account - and each one is a back door into your business. The Admin Account Cleanup finds and removes them. We audit privileged access across Microsoft 365, on-premises Active Directory when present, and cloud platforms like Google Workspace, Salesforce, and QuickBooks. We identify stale accounts for departed staff, shared admin logins with no individual accountability, and users whose privileges exceed their job. You approve every change before we make it, and you end up with a documented, least-privilege admin structure with clear ownership for every account that remains.
bestFor: Businesses that have gone through employee turnover or IT-provider changes without cleaning up access
Organizations that still rely on shared admin logins with no way to know who used them
Companies where nobody is sure who currently has administrative privileges
Businesses preparing for an audit, compliance review, or cyber insurance application
whatIsIncluded: Microsoft 365 admin account audit covering Global, Exchange, SharePoint, and Teams admins
On-premises Active Directory admin group review when applicable
Cloud platform admin audit across Google Workspace, Salesforce, QuickBooks, and more
Stale and shared account identification with risk documentation
Approved removal or demotion of unnecessary privileges with audit logging
Final admin inventory documenting ownership, purpose, and review date for every account
customerOutcomes: A complete inventory of every administrative account across your business platforms
Former-employee, shared, and unused admin access removed with documented approval
A least-privilege admin structure where each account maps to a person and a job
Dramatically reduced risk of insider misuse and post-termination access

name: Business Email Safety Check
summary: Review email authentication, MFA, mailbox forwarding, and obvious mailbox risk.
marketingHeadline: Business Email Safety Check from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Your business email is your digital front door, and if SPF, DKIM, and DMARC aren't configured correctly, anyone can send emails that appear to come from you. The Business Email Safety Check verifies your domain's email authentication, reviews your Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace security settings, audits every mailbox's forwarding rules for unauthorized exfiltration, and confirms MFA is actually enabled on email accounts. It catches the exact failures that lead to business email compromise, spam-flagged domains that hurt deliverability, and silent data leaks through forwarding. You get a straight-to-the-point report with the specific records and settings that need fixing.
bestFor: Businesses worried about scammers impersonating their domain to customers and partners
Organizations whose legitimate emails are landing in spam due to missing authentication
Companies that want to verify nobody has set up unauthorized mailbox forwarding
Businesses preparing for cyber insurance that requires verified email authentication
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC record audit with deliverability and spoofing implications
Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace email security configuration review
Mailbox forwarding-rule audit across all user mailboxes
MFA status verification on all email accounts
Plain-English email security report with prioritized fixes
customerOutcomes: Verified SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configuration that blocks domain spoofing
Discovery and removal of any unauthorized email forwarding or data-exfiltration rules
Confirmation that MFA protects every mailbox, closing the most common BEC path
Improved email deliverability because authentication records are correct

name: Basic Incident Readiness Checklist
summary: Create a lightweight incident contact sheet and first-response checklist.
marketingHeadline: Basic Incident Readiness Checklist from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When a security incident happens, panic and hesitation cause more damage than the attack itself. The Basic Incident Readiness Checklist gives your team a simple, usable playbook before something goes wrong. We build a step-by-step first-response checklist customized to your business size and systems: who does what, who to call, and how to contain the four most common scenarios - email compromise, ransomware, data breach, and service outage. This isn't a 50-page policy binder; it's a laminated, real-world checklist your staff can actually follow at 3 a.m. during an incident, and it satisfies the incident-response requirements many cyber insurers now demand.
bestFor: Businesses that have no incident response plan and want a practical starting point
Organizations that need a usable checklist rather than a dense policy document
Companies whose cyber insurance requires evidence of incident response readiness
Small teams that want clear roles and phone numbers defined before an emergency
whatIsIncluded: Incident classification guide with realistic examples for your business
Defined roles: incident commander, communications lead, and technical lead
Emergency contact list template covering insurance, legal, IT, and law enforcement
Step-by-step containment procedures for email compromise, ransomware, breach, and outage
Containment checklist covering isolate, preserve, notify, and begin recovery
Post-incident review template for lessons learned and improvements
customerOutcomes: A customized first-response checklist your team can execute under pressure
Clear roles, ownership, and escalation contacts defined before an incident happens
Faster containment in the critical first hour when decisions matter most
Incident-readiness documentation accepted by cyber insurance applications

name: Website Uptime Monitor Setup
summary: Set up basic website availability monitoring and alert routing.
marketingHeadline: Website Uptime Monitor Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A down website silently costs you leads, sales, and credibility - and most small businesses only find out when a customer calls. The Website Uptime Monitor Setup puts automated monitoring on your site so you know about problems before your customers do. We configure a professional uptime service that checks your site from multiple global locations every few minutes, alert you by email, SMS, or Slack when it goes down, and tune the alert rules so you aren't woken up by false alarms. We test that alerts actually fire, document the whole setup, and hand you a working early-warning system for your most important sales tool.

whatIsIncluded: Uptime monitoring service selection and configuration (UptimeRobot, BetterStack, or similar)

Email, SMS, and Slack or Teams alert routing
Alert-rule tuning to prevent false positives and alert fatigue
Monitoring setup documentation with escalation contacts
Initial monitoring and alert-testing period to confirm everything fires correctly
customerOutcomes: Automated downtime detection within minutes, from multiple locations worldwide
Instant alerts through the channels your team actually watches

name: Printer / Scanner Setup
summary: Install or troubleshoot a business printer or scanner workflow.
marketingHeadline: Printer / Scanner Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A printer that won't print or a scanner that won't scan is one of the most common daily frustrations in a small office - and usually a 20-minute fix hiding behind a confusing driver error. The Printer or Scanner Setup service handles it end to end. We connect the device to your network over wired or wireless, install the correct drivers on every workstation that needs access, configure scan-to-email or scan-to-folder so scanning actually saves time, set sensible defaults like duplex and paper size, and test printing and scanning from every machine so nothing is left half-working. Your team gets a device that just works, plus simple instructions for the tasks they do every day.

Businesses where printing or scanning only works on some computers
Companies that want scan-to-email or scan-to-folder configured properly
Teams tired of troubleshooting the same printer error on every workstation
whatIsIncluded: Wired or wireless network configuration for the printer or scanner
Driver installation and configuration on all designated workstations
Scan-to-email, scan-to-folder, or scan-to-cloud destination setup
Print queue, default settings, and duplex configuration
Functionality testing from every workstation including test prints and test scans
Simple user instructions for common printing and scanning tasks
customerOutcomes: Printing and scanning that work reliably from every designated workstation

name: PC Tune-Up / Cleanup
summary: Clean up startup items, updates, junk apps, and basic performance issues.
marketingHeadline: PC Tune-Up / Cleanup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Slow computers aren't a hardware problem as often as you'd think - they're usually a build-up of startup programs, junk files, outdated software, and bloatware. The PC Tune-Up and Cleanup service gives a sluggish workstation a measurable performance boost without spending thousands on new hardware. We clear temporary files and old downloads, disable unnecessary startup items that slow boot times, install pending Windows and application updates, remove software nobody uses, and benchmark the machine before and after so you can see the real improvement in boot time, available memory, and disk speed. For a business extending the life of existing computers, this is the cheapest performance upgrade available.
bestFor: Businesses with workstations that have gotten noticeably slower over time
Organizations that want to extend the life of existing hardware before buying replacements
Staff members frustrated by long boot times and sluggish everyday performance
Companies that want measurable before-and-after proof of a performance fix
whatIsIncluded: Disk analysis and cleanup of temporary files, old downloads, and recycle bin contents
Startup program review and optimization for faster boot times
Installation of pending Windows and application updates
Identification and removal of unnecessary or bloatware software
Before-and-after performance benchmarking (boot time, memory, disk speed)
Maintenance recommendations to keep the machine fast
customerOutcomes: Measurably faster boot and everyday performance with benchmark proof
Recovered disk space from files and applications that were never needed
A cleaner, more secure system with updates and fewer attack surfaces

name: M365 Security Assessment
summary: Microsoft 365-focused security configuration and risk review.
marketingHeadline: M365 Security Assessment from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Your Microsoft 365 tenant holds your email, files, identities, and collaboration - and its default settings aren't secure enough for most businesses. The M365 Security Assessment is a focused review of everything that matters in your tenant: MFA and Conditional Access, admin role assignments, external sharing and guest access, email protection, retention and backup posture, and identity risk configurations. We inspect the actual settings in your tenant (not a questionnaire), document what's configured versus what Microsoft recommends, and rank every gap by risk so you can fix the dangerous items first. It's the definitive answer to 'how secure is our Microsoft 365, really?'
bestFor: Businesses running Microsoft 365 that haven't had a security review of their tenant
Organizations that inherited a tenant from a previous provider or employee
Companies concerned about external sharing, guest access, or admin sprawl
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance reviews that cover cloud security
whatIsIncluded: MFA and Conditional Access policy review in your actual tenant
Global and delegated admin role assignment audit
External sharing and guest access review across SharePoint, OneDrive, and Teams
Email protection review covering anti-phishing, anti-spam, and spoofing controls
Retention, backup, and data-loss-prevention posture review
Identity risk configuration review (legacy auth, risky sign-ins, stale accounts)
Risk-ranked findings report with tenant-specific remediation guidance
customerOutcomes: A tenant-specific picture of your M365 security posture with real settings as evidence
The most dangerous gaps (legacy auth, admin sprawl, wide-open external sharing) identified first
Clear, actionable changes mapped to your actual tenant configuration
Insurance-ready documentation of your cloud security controls

Major remediation beyond the purchased scope
Emergency after-hours response unless the emergency product is purchased
Legal, tax, insurance, or regulatory advice

name: Small Business Ransomware Readiness Review
summary: Review ransomware-relevant controls such as backups, MFA, endpoint security, admin rights, and recovery.
marketingHeadline: Small Business Ransomware Readiness Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Ransomware doesn't just hit big companies - small businesses are the favorite target because they're easier and less likely to have tested backups. The Small Business Ransomware Readiness Review checks the specific controls that decide whether you survive an attack or shut down: are your backups real, tested, and off-site; is MFA stopping account takeover; is endpoint protection active; do users have admin rights they shouldn't; and is there a documented recovery path? We assess each control, show you the gaps in plain English, and rank the fixes by how much they improve your odds of a fast recovery. This review focuses on the handful of things that actually determine ransomware outcomes.
bestFor: Businesses worried about ransomware but unsure whether their backups would actually save them
Organizations with backups that have never been tested
Companies where users have local admin rights or MFA isn't enforced
Businesses that want to understand ransomware survival odds before an attack
whatIsIncluded: Backup assessment: does it exist, does it run, is it off-site, and has it been tested
MFA coverage review across email and critical cloud accounts
Endpoint protection and patch posture review
Local admin rights review across workstations
Recovery documentation and incident-response readiness check
Ransomware Readiness Scorecard with prioritized hardening steps
customerOutcomes: A clear answer to 'would we survive ransomware' with evidence for each control
Tested-backup gaps identified before you need the backup
A prioritized hardening list ranked by recovery impact
Documented ransomware readiness for insurance applications

We understand you can't spend like an enterprise - so we focus on the highest-impact protections that fit a nonprofit budget.

name: Vendor Access Review
summary: Review vendor accounts, shared access, remote access, and access removal process.
marketingHeadline: Vendor Access Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Every vendor with a login into your systems is a potential entry point - and most small businesses have no idea how many vendors have access, to what, or whether that access was ever revoked. The Vendor Access Review maps your vendor relationships to actual system access: who has remote access, which shared accounts exist, what third parties can reach, and what happens to access when a vendor relationship ends. We identify vendor accounts that should have been removed years ago, shared credentials that vendors use that create accountability gaps, and remote-access paths that bypass your security controls. You get a complete vendor-access map and a cleanup plan with documented approvals.
bestFor: Businesses that have worked with multiple vendors, contractors, or IT providers over time
Organizations where vendors use shared or generic accounts
Companies that aren't sure which third parties currently have remote access
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance reviews covering third-party risk
whatIsIncluded: Complete inventory of vendor accounts and their system access
Shared and generic vendor credential review
Remote access path review (VPN, RDP, remote support tools)
Identification of stale vendor accounts that should be revoked
Vendor Access Map and prioritized cleanup plan
customerOutcomes: A complete map of which vendors can access what - and which shouldn't anymore
Shared vendor credentials documented and remediation path defined
Stale vendor access removed with approved, logged changes
Third-party risk evidence ready for insurance and compliance reviews

name: Admin Privilege Review
summary: Review high-privilege accounts, role assignments, and excessive access.
marketingHeadline: Admin Privilege Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Admin privileges are the crown jewels of your IT environment - and the accounts that hold them are what attackers target first. The Admin Privilege Review digs into every high-privilege account in your business: who has administrator rights in Microsoft 365, on servers, on domain controllers, and on business-critical cloud apps. We check role assignments against actual job needs, flag excessive or inherited permissions, identify break-glass and shared admin accounts, and assess how changes to privileged access are approved and tracked. You end up with a documented picture of who can do what at the highest levels - and a plan to move toward least privilege without breaking daily operations.
bestFor: Organizations with multiple admins, past IT providers, or unclear role assignments
Businesses that have given out admin rights casually over the years
Companies that don't have a documented map of who holds elevated access
Organizations preparing for audits, insurance, or compliance reviews
whatIsIncluded: High-privilege account inventory across Microsoft 365, servers, and cloud apps
Role assignment review against actual job responsibilities
Excessive, stale, and shared privileged account identification
Break-glass and emergency access account review
Least-privilege remediation roadmap with documented approvals
customerOutcomes: A complete map of every account with elevated access and why it has it
Excessive or unnecessary admin rights identified and removed with approval
Reduced attack surface where compromise of one account no longer means full control
Privileged access evidence ready for audit and insurance review

name: MFA Enforcement Project
summary: Plan and implement broader MFA rollout for selected systems.
marketingHeadline: MFA Enforcement Project from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Enabling MFA on one account is easy; enforcing it across every user and system without locking anyone out is a project. The MFA Enforcement Project plans and implements a broader MFA rollout across the systems that matter to your business. We start with a coverage assessment, then build a rollout plan that includes Microsoft 365 Conditional Access enforcement, onboarding of every user with clear instructions, and coverage of critical third-party platforms like banking, payroll, and your domain registrar. We handle the coordination, the enrollment support, and the verification - so MFA gets turned on everywhere, staff stay productive, and nobody gets stuck. When the project is done, MFA isn't optional anymore; it's the rule.
bestFor: Businesses ready to enforce MFA everywhere but worried about rollout friction

Companies where MFA is 'suggested' but not required across all users

whatIsIncluded: MFA coverage assessment across all business systems

name: Password Manager Rollout
summary: Deploy a business password manager and train users on safer credential practices.
marketingHeadline: Password Manager Rollout from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A password manager is the single most practical tool for eliminating weak and reused passwords - but only if it's deployed properly and people actually use it. The Password Manager Rollout goes beyond installing software: we help you select the right platform for your team (Bitwarden, 1Password, or Keeper), configure the organization with shared vaults and permissions, migrate critical credentials from spreadsheets and browsers, and train every user on day-to-day use. Staff stop reusing passwords, shared accounts get controlled by the business instead of shared in a spreadsheet, and you get visibility into credential hygiene that didn't exist before. It's the password hygiene project, done so it sticks.

Organizations that want shared team credentials without insecure sharing
Companies that bought a password manager but never actually deployed it properly

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope: "Password Manager Rollout" for [customer]. Review deploy a business password manager and train users on safer credential practices. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.

Remote session: connect to customer environment via ScreenConnect or Teams. Share screen and review current password practices — shared accounts, password spreadsheets, browser-saved passwords, and password reuse.

M365 password policy audit: navigate to admin.microsoft.com > Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy. Document current password expiration, complexity requirements, account lockout threshold. Screenshot settings.
Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Password Manager Rollout. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.

triage: Confirm purchase scope: "Password Manager Rollout" for [customer]. Review deploy a business password manager and train users on safer credential practices. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.
Pre-work access check: verify customer has provided or confirmed admin access to required systems. If admin credentials are missing, request before proceeding — do not start without proper access.
Gather baseline: collect current documentation, previous IT provider notes, existing configurations, known issues, and any urgency or compliance factors. Note any deadlines or insurance requirements.

Create ticket: log in internal system with product ID "password_manager_rollout", customer name, scope boundaries, expected deliverables, exclusions, and follow-up plan. Assign appropriate technician based on skill set.
delivery: Remote session: connect to customer environment via ScreenConnect or Teams. Share screen and review current password practices — shared accounts, password spreadsheets, browser-saved passwords, and password reuse.

M365 password policy audit: navigate to admin.microsoft.com > Settings > Org settings > Security & privacy. Document current password expiration, complexity requirements, account lockout threshold. Screenshot settings.

Compromised account scan: run https://haveibeenpwned.com/DomainSearch on customer email domain. For each exposed account, note breach source, date, and exposed data type. Flag accounts needing immediate password change.

Shared account inventory: check shared mailbox configuration in Exchange Admin Center. Check for generic accounts (info@, sales@, office@). Review for any user accounts shared by multiple staff — document all findings.

Password manager assessment: evaluate customer's current state (no manager, personal tools, business manager). Compare Bitwarden Teams, 1Password Business, and Keeper — recommend best fit based on team size, devices, budget. Demo recommended tool.
Findings documentation: compile Password Security Scorecard with sections: Policy Settings, Compromised Accounts, Shared Accounts, Manager Readiness. Rate each section Green/Yellow/Red.
Customer review: present findings via 15-minute video call or detailed email. Walk through each finding, answer questions, discuss recommended next steps. Get acknowledgement of receipt.
documentation: Record all findings, configurations, changes, and decisions made during the Password Manager Rollout engagement. Use structured format: date, action, result, follow-up needed.
Create plain-English customer summary tailored to a non-technical audience. Explain what was done, what was found (if assessment), what was changed (if setup), and what it means for the business.
Include visual evidence: screenshots of configurations before and after, network diagrams or topology maps if applicable, benchmark results, coverage maps, or any other visual that adds clarity.

Document out-of-scope observations separately. If any issues were discovered outside the purchased scope, note them with a brief description and recommended follow-up action. Do not act on them without customer approval.

Security rule: never store passwords, recovery codes, MFA seeds, API keys, private keys, credit card numbers, or unredacted sensitive data in any documentation. Confirm this before closing the ticket.
qa: Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Password Manager Rollout. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Secret audit: review all documentation, notes, and screenshots for stored credentials, API keys, recovery codes, or sensitive data. Remove or redact immediately if found.
Verify deliverable completeness: is the customer summary ready? Are all reports formatted correctly? Are screenshots included? Are recommendations prioritized?
Category-specific check: verify service-specific quality criteria are met.
Flag follow-up items: identify any recommended next steps, whether optional, recommended, or urgent. Tag items that should be addressed within 30 days vs longer-term.
closeout: Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.
Attach or link all supporting materials: screenshots, diagrams, guides, policy documents, configuration exports. Ensure all links work and are accessible to the customer.
Recommend next-step services: based on findings and customer needs, suggest: Security Awareness Training, Incident Response Plan, Monthly Care Plan.
Revoke temporary access: if temporary admin access was granted for the engagement, confirm it has been revoked. If the customer provided credentials, remind them to rotate passwords if appropriate.

Schedule follow-up: if recommendations include specific actions, schedule a reminder to follow up in 30-60 days. For monthly plan customers, confirm next recurring engagement date. For bundles, confirm all components were delivered.

name: Email Security Hardening
summary: Configure practical anti-spoofing, anti-phishing, and email safety improvements.
marketingHeadline: Email Security Hardening from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Email is the attack surface attackers exploit most - through spoofed domains, phishing, and misconfigured authentication. The Email Security Hardening service configures practical, high-impact email protections rather than just reviewing them. We correct your SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records so your domain can't be easily impersonated, tighten Microsoft 365 anti-phishing and anti-spam policies including impersonation protection, review mailbox rules for compromise indicators, and confirm MFA protects every mailbox. We make the changes that meaningfully reduce phishing and business email compromise, verify delivery still works, and document what we configured. It's email security turned from a recommendation into a completed configuration.
bestFor: Businesses that want email protections actually configured, not just reviewed
Organizations whose domain is being spoofed or whose email lands in spam
Companies with Microsoft 365 that never customized anti-phishing settings
Businesses hardening their email before insurance or compliance review
whatIsIncluded: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC correction and verification
Microsoft 365 anti-phishing policy configuration including impersonation protection
Mailbox rule audit for compromise indicators
customerOutcomes: A domain that attackers can't easily impersonate in email
Hardened Microsoft 365 policies that filter more phishing before it reaches inboxes
Compromise indicators like suspicious forwarding rules identified and removed
Documented email security configuration you can show insurers and auditors
whatIsNotIncluded: Hardware, licenses, subscriptions, permits, or third-party service fees unless explicitly included
Major remediation beyond the purchased scope
Emergency after-hours response unless the emergency product is purchased
Legal, tax, insurance, or regulatory advice
Credential collection through public forms

A contact person who can answer business and technical questions

Permission to document findings and recommendations

name: Endpoint Protection Rollout
summary: Deploy or improve endpoint protection tooling and monitoring process.
marketingHeadline: Endpoint Protection Rollout from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Endpoint protection is only effective if it's deployed on every device, configured properly, and actually being monitored. The Endpoint Protection Rollout ensures your business computers - Windows and Mac - are running a real, current, centrally managed endpoint security solution. We assess what's currently on each device (including the dangerous state of 'nothing' or expired consumer antivirus), select an appropriate business solution, deploy it across your fleet, configure detection and response settings, and set up a monitoring process so alerts aren't ignored. Your endpoints stop being the soft target attackers rely on and start being defended, managed, and accounted for.
bestFor: Businesses with a mix of unprotected or inconsistently protected devices
Organizations relying on free or expired consumer antivirus
Companies that want centrally managed endpoint security across their fleet
Businesses preparing for insurance that requires endpoint protection
whatIsIncluded: Current endpoint protection state assessment across all devices
Solution selection and licensing guidance (Microsoft Defender for Business or similar)
Central deployment across Windows and Mac workstations
Monitoring process setup so security events aren't missed
Deployment documentation and fleet-wide coverage verification
customerOutcomes: Every business device running current, managed endpoint protection
A centrally managed view of your fleet's security status
Detection and response that flags real threats instead of silent gaps
Insurance- and audit-ready endpoint coverage evidence

name: Local Admin Removal Project
summary: Reduce unnecessary local admin privileges across selected workstations.
marketingHeadline: Local Admin Removal Project from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When every user has local administrator rights on their computer, a single click on a malicious file can take down the whole machine - and your data. The Local Admin Removal Project reduces these privileges across your selected workstations without disrupting productivity. We identify which users actually need admin rights, plan the removal so legitimate software installs still work, execute the change across the fleet, and handle the support tickets that follow so the transition doesn't break your staff. Removing local admin is one of the most effective, least expensive hardening measures available - and doing it as a planned project instead of a surprise is the only way it succeeds.
bestFor: Businesses where every user can install software and change system settings
Organizations that want a high-impact hardening win with minimal disruption
Companies that have dealt with malware infections that started with local admin
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance that limits admin rights
whatIsIncluded: Current local admin rights assessment across selected workstations
Legitimate software install and update needs analysis
Local admin removal plan with exception management
Fleet-wide execution of the privilege change
Post-change support for staff affected by the transition
Documentation of who retains admin rights and why
customerOutcomes: Local admin privileges removed across the fleet, shrinking the malware blast radius
Legitimate software installs still working through approved processes
A managed exception list instead of everyone-has-admin by default
A documented hardening improvement that insurers and auditors recognize

name: BitLocker Encryption Rollout
summary: Enable or verify disk encryption on supported business devices.
marketingHeadline: BitLocker Encryption Rollout from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A stolen or lost laptop containing customer data is a breach - unless the drive is encrypted. The BitLocker Encryption Rollout enables full-disk encryption on your supported business devices so that if a computer is lost or stolen, the data on it is unreadable. We verify which devices support BitLocker (and review Mac equivalents), enable encryption properly with recovery keys stored somewhere safe, confirm it's actually protecting data rather than just enabled, and document the recovery key locations so you never get locked out of your own data. Disk encryption is a core insurance and compliance requirement, and this rollout makes it a configured, verified reality.
bestFor: Businesses with laptops that travel, remote workers, or field staff
Organizations that handle customer, payment, or health data on portable devices
Companies that aren't sure whether their drives are actually encrypted
Businesses meeting insurance or compliance requirements for data-at-rest protection

name: DNS Filtering Setup
summary: Configure protective DNS filtering where appropriate.
marketingHeadline: DNS Filtering Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: DNS filtering blocks dangerous websites before your users even reach them, catching phishing, malware, and ransomware delivery at the network level. The DNS Filtering Setup configures protective DNS for your business where it's appropriate, creating a first line of defense that works even when users click something they shouldn't. We evaluate your current DNS setup, recommend an appropriate filtering service, configure it so business traffic is protected while web browsing stays functional, and handle exception requests so legitimate sites aren't blocked. DNS filtering is invisible to your staff but actively blocking threats every day - one of the highest-value, lowest-friction security controls available.
bestFor: Businesses that want network-level protection beyond endpoint software
Organizations that want to block known-malicious sites without blocking productivity
Companies preparing for insurance that rewards layered security controls
Businesses that want an always-on safety net for click-prone staff

Category and policy configuration to balance security with productivity
Exception handling for legitimate blocked sites
Documentation and verification that filtering is active
customerOutcomes: Network-level blocking of known phishing, malware, and ransomware domains

Another layered control documented for insurance and compliance

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope: "Incident Response Plan Starter" for [customer]. Review create a practical first-response plan for common security incidents. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.

Pre-work preparation: review customer intake responses, current documentation, and any previous service history. Prepare session with required tools: M365 Defender, Nessus/OpenVAS, Microsoft Secure Score, MXToolbox, HaveIBeenPwned. Confirm customer has provided required access.
Initial assessment: connect to customer environment via secure remote session. Document current state before making any changes — take screenshots, note current settings, record baseline metrics.
Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Incident Response Plan Starter. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.

triage: Confirm purchase scope: "Incident Response Plan Starter" for [customer]. Review create a practical first-response plan for common security incidents. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.
Pre-work access check: verify customer has provided or confirmed admin access to required systems. If admin credentials are missing, request before proceeding — do not start without proper access.
Gather baseline: collect current documentation, previous IT provider notes, existing configurations, known issues, and any urgency or compliance factors. Note any deadlines or insurance requirements.

Create ticket: log in internal system with product ID "incident_response_plan_starter", customer name, scope boundaries, expected deliverables, exclusions, and follow-up plan. Assign appropriate technician based on skill set.
delivery: Pre-work preparation: review customer intake responses, current documentation, and any previous service history. Prepare session with required tools: M365 Defender, Nessus/OpenVAS, Microsoft Secure Score, MXToolbox, HaveIBeenPwned. Confirm customer has provided required access.
Initial assessment: connect to customer environment via secure remote session. Document current state before making any changes — take screenshots, note current settings, record baseline metrics.

Execute Incident Response Plan Starter assessment per scope. Systematically review each area defined in the scope: Create a practical first-response plan for common security incidents.. Check settings, configurations, and behaviors against security best practices and industry standards.

Findings documentation: as each area is reviewed, document findings in real-time. Categorize by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low) and by area. Screenshot evidence for each finding. Note potential business impact.

Technical verification: test all changes, configurations, or improvements made. For assessments: verify all findings are accurate and evidence-based. For setup/installation: verify all systems function correctly. For cleanup: verify no unintended removals occurred.

Prepare deliverables: compile all documentation, screenshots, configuration notes, and recommendations into a structured deliverable package. Format for customer readability — use plain English, highlight key findings, and prioritize recommendations.

Customer walkthrough: schedule 15-30 minute session to walk through findings/deliverables with the customer. Answer questions, provide context, and explain next steps. Get customer acknowledgment of service completion.
documentation: Record all findings, configurations, changes, and decisions made during the Incident Response Plan Starter engagement. Use structured format: date, action, result, follow-up needed.
Create plain-English customer summary tailored to a non-technical audience. Explain what was done, what was found (if assessment), what was changed (if setup), and what it means for the business.
Include visual evidence: screenshots of configurations before and after, network diagrams or topology maps if applicable, benchmark results, coverage maps, or any other visual that adds clarity.

Document out-of-scope observations separately. If any issues were discovered outside the purchased scope, note them with a brief description and recommended follow-up action. Do not act on them without customer approval.

Security rule: never store passwords, recovery codes, MFA seeds, API keys, private keys, credit card numbers, or unredacted sensitive data in any documentation. Confirm this before closing the ticket.
qa: Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Incident Response Plan Starter. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Secret audit: review all documentation, notes, and screenshots for stored credentials, API keys, recovery codes, or sensitive data. Remove or redact immediately if found.
Verify deliverable completeness: is the customer summary ready? Are all reports formatted correctly? Are screenshots included? Are recommendations prioritized?
Category-specific check: verify service-specific quality criteria are met.
Flag follow-up items: identify any recommended next steps, whether optional, recommended, or urgent. Tag items that should be addressed within 30 days vs longer-term.
closeout: Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.
Attach or link all supporting materials: screenshots, diagrams, guides, policy documents, configuration exports. Ensure all links work and are accessible to the customer.
Recommend next-step services: based on findings and customer needs, suggest: Security Awareness Training, Incident Response Plan, Monthly Care Plan.
Revoke temporary access: if temporary admin access was granted for the engagement, confirm it has been revoked. If the customer provided credentials, remind them to rotate passwords if appropriate.

Record internal notes: add ticket notes with key technical details for future reference. Note any customer-specific configurations, access methods, or environmental details that will help on future engagements.

Schedule follow-up: if recommendations include specific actions, schedule a reminder to follow up in 30-60 days. For monthly plan customers, confirm next recurring engagement date. For bundles, confirm all components were delivered.

For regulated data, minimize access and store only required evidence

name: Cyber Insurance Readiness Package
summary: Review common cyber insurance controls, evidence gaps, and remediation priorities.
marketingHeadline: Cyber Insurance Readiness Package from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Cyber insurance applications are increasingly strict - and many small businesses get denied, quoted higher premiums, or hit with coverage carve-outs because of common gaps like missing MFA, untested backups, or no documented policies. The Cyber Insurance Readiness Package gets your business in a defensible position before you apply. We review the controls insurers commonly require (MFA, backup, endpoint protection, admin access, incident response, training), help you address the gaps within scope, and compile the evidence insurers ask for. You approach the application with documentation instead of hoping, which improves approval odds, premium levels, and coverage terms.
bestFor: Businesses applying for cyber insurance and unsure what the questionnaire means
Organizations that were denied coverage or quoted high premiums due to gaps
Companies that want to strengthen controls before their renewal
Businesses that want a documented readiness posture rather than best-effort answers
whatIsIncluded: Review of common cyber insurance control requirements
MFA, backup, endpoint, admin access, and training control assessment
In-scope remediation of the gaps most insurers require
Readiness summary documenting your controls and remaining gaps
Guidance for completing the insurance application accurately
customerOutcomes: A documented, evidence-backed position when applying for cyber insurance
The most common coverage-denial gaps addressed before you apply
Confidence in answering the insurance questionnaire accurately
Better approval odds and, in many cases, better premiums and coverage terms
whatIsNotIncluded: Hardware, licenses, subscriptions, permits, or third-party service fees unless explicitly included
Major remediation beyond the purchased scope
Emergency after-hours response unless the emergency product is purchased
Legal, tax, insurance, or regulatory advice
Credential collection through public forms
customerPrerequisites: Authorized decision maker approval
A contact person who can answer business and technical questions
Safe access coordination when admin work is required
Permission to document findings and recommendations

name: Security Awareness Lunch & Learn
summary: Short training session for phishing, passwords, MFA, and safe employee habits.
marketingHeadline: Security Awareness Lunch & Learn from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A one-hour lunch-and-learn is one of the most cost-effective security investments a small business can make - because your staff are the first line of defense. The Security Awareness Lunch & Learn delivers a practical, engaging training session on phishing, passwords, MFA, and safe everyday habits, customized to your team and the threats they actually face. We use real-world examples and interactive discussion rather than slides nobody remembers, and every attendee leaves with a cheat sheet they can actually use. It's perfect for kicking off a security culture or refreshing staff who've become complacent.
bestFor: Businesses that want a high-impact, low-cost staff awareness boost
Organizations that haven't done any security training and want to start
Companies with staff who've fallen for phishing or weak-password habits
Teams that need a refresher that's engaging rather than boring
whatIsIncluded: Customized training session covering phishing, passwords, MFA, and safe habits
Real-world examples relevant to your business and industry
Printable reference materials for every attendee
Session delivery on-site or remote to fit your schedule
customerOutcomes: Staff who recognize phishing and report it instead of clicking
Better password and MFA habits across the team
A documented training event for insurance and compliance
A foundation for ongoing security culture

name: Owner/Admin Security Training
summary: Focused security training for owners, admins, and managers.
marketingHeadline: Owner/Admin Security Training from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Owners and administrators hold the keys to your business - and their accounts are the highest-value targets. The Owner/Admin Security Training is focused, technical security training for the people who manage your systems: the business owner, the office manager who handles admin accounts, and anyone with elevated access. We cover the specific attacks aimed at privileged users (phishing targeting admins, password attacks, session theft), how to protect admin accounts with MFA and least privilege, how to review security alerts and audit logs, and how to handle a suspected compromise. This is training for the people whose compromise would be catastrophic - so they stop being the weakest link.
bestFor: Business owners who personally hold admin accounts
Office managers or staff who administer email, domains, and cloud apps
Organizations where one person's compromise would be catastrophic
Businesses that want their privileged users to know how to spot admin-targeted attacks
whatIsIncluded: Training tailored to owners and administrative users
Admin-specific attack awareness: spear phishing, password attacks, session theft
MFA and least-privilege best practices for privileged accounts
Security alert and audit log interpretation
Practical reference materials for daily admin work
customerOutcomes: Privileged users who recognize attacks aimed specifically at them
Protected admin accounts with MFA and least-privilege habits
Staff who can interpret security alerts instead of ignoring them
A documented training event strengthening your highest-risk accounts

summary: Clean up stale users, licenses, groups, mailbox delegation, and insecure collaboration settings.
marketingHeadline: Microsoft 365 Tenant Cleanup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Over the years, Microsoft 365 tenants accumulate stale users, wrong licenses, orphaned groups, mailbox delegation that shouldn't exist, and insecure collaboration settings - often left behind by former employees and past IT providers. name: Shared Mailbox Cleanup
summary: Review shared mailbox permissions, delegation, stale access, and mailbox usage.
marketingHeadline: Shared Mailbox Cleanup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Shared mailboxes quietly accumulate permissions, delegation, and stale access - former employees who can still read them, users with Full Access who shouldn't have it, and mailboxes that nobody uses anymore. The Shared Mailbox Cleanup reviews every shared mailbox in your tenant and its permission structure. We identify which shared mailboxes are still needed, document who has access and what kind, flag stale and excessive permissions, and clean up what you approve. You get a documented picture of your shared mailbox environment with the access risk removed - because a shared mailbox with the wrong people in it is a data leak waiting to happen.

name: Departing Employee Lockdown
summary: Disable or secure a departing worker account and preserve needed business data.
marketingHeadline: Departing Employee Lockdown from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A departing employee's account is a security risk the moment they leave - whether they leave on good terms or bad. We handle the account hygiene so you're not left wondering whether a former employee still has access to email, files, or apps. We also preserve important data - mailbox content, OneDrive files, and anything the business needs - before access is cut. The account is locked down fast, and the data is saved.

name: Lifecycle Replacement Plan
summary: Create a staged replacement plan for aging computers and devices.
marketingHeadline: Lifecycle Replacement Plan from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Hardware fails on its own schedule - and without a replacement plan, businesses make emergency purchases, scramble for budget, and run a mix of aging, unreliable devices. The Lifecycle Replacement Plan creates a staged replacement roadmap for your computers and devices. We inventory the fleet, assess age and condition, and build a phased replacement schedule spread over multiple years so purchases are planned and budgeted rather than panicked. You get a practical plan that turns hardware replacement from a crisis into a scheduled, budgeted process.

name: Data Transfer Service
summary: Move selected user data from old computer to new computer.
marketingHeadline: Data Transfer Service from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Moving to a new computer usually means losing something - an overlooked folder, a browser bookmark, a configuration, or a document that lived only in one place. The Data Transfer Service moves your selected user data from an old computer to a new one completely and safely. We identify what matters - documents, emails, browser data, and application settings - and migrate it to the new machine with verification that everything arrived. You get your new computer with your data intact and nothing left behind on the old one. It's the part of computer replacement that's usually done wrong, done right.

summary: Onsite or guided review of Wi-Fi coverage, dead zones, and upgrade path.
marketingHeadline: Wi-Fi Coverage Check from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Dead zones, dropped connections, and slow spots are the most common complaints in any office - and they're rarely about the internet connection itself. The Wi-Fi Coverage Check is an onsite or guided review of your wireless coverage that pinpoints exactly where Wi-Fi is weak and why. We test signal strength across your space, identify dead zones and interference sources, assess whether your current access points are positioned and configured correctly, and map the path to better coverage - whether that's repositioning, adding access points, or upgrading hardware. You get a coverage map and a practical upgrade path instead of guessing why Wi-Fi keeps dropping.

Signal strength testing across your space
Access point placement and configuration review
customerOutcomes: A clear map of your actual Wi-Fi coverage and problem areas
The real cause of dead zones identified - placement, interference, or capacity
A practical, prioritized path to better coverage
No more guesswork about why Wi-Fi keeps dropping

name: Guest Wi-Fi Review
summary: Review guest network separation, password practices, and business/guest isolation.
marketingHeadline: Guest Wi-Fi Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Guest Wi-Fi that shares your business network is a back door - guests, customers, and vendors on the same network as your computers and files can reach sensitive systems. The Guest Wi-Fi Review examines how your guest network is set up and whether it's actually separated from your business systems. We check whether guests and business traffic are isolated, review guest password practices, and assess the risk of current configuration. You get a clear answer to the question every business should be able to answer: are our guests on our business network?
bestFor: Businesses that offer Wi-Fi to customers, clients, or visitors
Organizations unsure whether guest and business networks are separated
Companies with guest Wi-Fi sharing the same network as staff computers
Businesses preparing for security or compliance reviews
whatIsIncluded: Business and guest traffic isolation assessment
Guest password and access practice review
customerOutcomes: A clear answer on whether guests can reach business systems
Guest and business traffic properly isolated where needed
Safe guest Wi-Fi password and access practices
Documented separation for security reviews

fulfillmentWorkflow: Confirm purchase scope: "Guest Wi-Fi Review" for [customer]. Review review guest network separation, password practices, and business/guest isolation. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.

Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Guest Wi-Fi Review. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.

triage: Confirm purchase scope: "Guest Wi-Fi Review" for [customer]. Review review guest network separation, password practices, and business/guest isolation. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.
Pre-work access check: verify customer has provided or confirmed admin access to required systems. If admin credentials are missing, request before proceeding — do not start without proper access.
Gather baseline: collect current documentation, previous IT provider notes, existing configurations, known issues, and any urgency or compliance factors. Note any deadlines or insurance requirements.

Create ticket: log in internal system with product ID "guest_wi_fi_review", customer name, scope boundaries, expected deliverables, exclusions, and follow-up plan. Assign appropriate technician based on skill set.
delivery: Pre-work preparation: review customer intake responses, current documentation, and any previous service history. Prepare session with required tools: UniFi Controller, Wi-Fi analyzer (NetSpot/Ekahau), cable tester, toner, laptop with management access. Confirm customer has provided required access.
Initial assessment: connect to customer environment via secure remote session. Document current state before making any changes — take screenshots, note current settings, record baseline metrics.
Execute Guest Wi-Fi Review per scope. Perform on-site work at customer location: access network equipment, run diagnostics, make configuration changes per plan. Take before and after screenshots.
Verify improvements: test connectivity from multiple locations, measure speed/performance, check for dead zones (Wi-Fi), verify VLAN separation, test failover if applicable.

Technical verification: test all changes, configurations, or improvements made. For assessments: verify all findings are accurate and evidence-based. For setup/installation: verify all systems function correctly. For cleanup: verify no unintended removals occurred.

Prepare deliverables: compile all documentation, screenshots, configuration notes, and recommendations into a structured deliverable package. Format for customer readability — use plain English, highlight key findings, and prioritize recommendations.

Customer walkthrough: schedule 15-30 minute session to walk through findings/deliverables with the customer. Answer questions, provide context, and explain next steps. Get customer acknowledgment of service completion.
documentation: Record all findings, configurations, changes, and decisions made during the Guest Wi-Fi Review engagement. Use structured format: date, action, result, follow-up needed.
Create plain-English customer summary tailored to a non-technical audience. Explain what was done, what was found (if assessment), what was changed (if setup), and what it means for the business.
Include visual evidence: screenshots of configurations before and after, network diagrams or topology maps if applicable, benchmark results, coverage maps, or any other visual that adds clarity.

Document out-of-scope observations separately. If any issues were discovered outside the purchased scope, note them with a brief description and recommended follow-up action. Do not act on them without customer approval.

Security rule: never store passwords, recovery codes, MFA seeds, API keys, private keys, credit card numbers, or unredacted sensitive data in any documentation. Confirm this before closing the ticket.
qa: Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for Guest Wi-Fi Review. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Secret audit: review all documentation, notes, and screenshots for stored credentials, API keys, recovery codes, or sensitive data. Remove or redact immediately if found.
Verify deliverable completeness: is the customer summary ready? Are all reports formatted correctly? Are screenshots included? Are recommendations prioritized?
Category-specific check: verify network connectivity and coverage meet scope requirements.
Flag follow-up items: identify any recommended next steps, whether optional, recommended, or urgent. Tag items that should be addressed within 30 days vs longer-term.
closeout: Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.
Attach or link all supporting materials: screenshots, diagrams, guides, policy documents, configuration exports. Ensure all links work and are accessible to the customer.
Recommend next-step services: based on findings and customer needs, suggest: related bundles, monthly plans, or category-specific follow-up services.
Revoke temporary access: if temporary admin access was granted for the engagement, confirm it has been revoked. If the customer provided credentials, remind them to rotate passwords if appropriate.

Record internal notes: add ticket notes with key technical details for future reference. Note any customer-specific configurations, access methods, or environmental details that will help on future engagements.

Schedule follow-up: if recommendations include specific actions, schedule a reminder to follow up in 30-60 days. For monthly plan customers, confirm next recurring engagement date. For bundles, confirm all components were delivered.

name: Camera Network Readiness Check
summary: Determine whether the current network can support cameras and recording needs.
marketingHeadline: Camera Network Readiness Check from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Security cameras need a network that can support them - enough bandwidth, stable connections, and the right structure - and discovering that during installation is the wrong time to find out. The Camera Network Readiness Check determines whether your current network can support cameras and recording before you buy a single camera. We assess your network capacity, bandwidth, wiring, Wi-Fi suitability, and whether you have the right infrastructure for NVR recording and remote access. You get a clear go/no-go assessment with the specific gaps to address before deployment. It's the planning step that prevents a camera installation from turning into a network project.
bestFor: Businesses planning to install security cameras
Organizations that want to know if their network can handle recording
Companies that want to avoid a failed camera installation
Businesses planning camera systems across a large or outdoor space

Wi-Fi suitability assessment for wireless cameras
Camera readiness report with gaps and recommendations

Specific gaps identified before you buy equipment

Avoidance of a failed camera installation

name: Outdoor Wi-Fi Planning Visit
summary: Plan outdoor AP placement, power, wiring, weatherproofing, and coverage validation.
marketingHeadline: Outdoor Wi-Fi Planning Visit from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Outdoor Wi-Fi is a different challenge than indoor - weather, power, cable runs, and coverage over open space all need planning. The Outdoor Wi-Fi Planning Visit plans your outdoor access point deployment properly: placement, power, wiring, weatherproofing, and coverage validation. We walk the site, determine where access points should go for the coverage you need, plan the power and cabling requirements, and consider weatherproofing for Maine's environment. You get a deployment plan for outdoor Wi-Fi that works - instead of access points installed in the wrong place, failing in the weather, or leaving dead zones.
bestFor: Businesses with yards, lots, marinas, warehouses, or outdoor spaces needing Wi-Fi
Organizations planning outdoor access point installation
Companies that need coverage planned before equipment is purchased
Businesses in Maine where weatherproofing is essential

Access points placed where they deliver the coverage you need

name: Firewall Configuration Review
summary: Review firewall rules, remote access, segmentation, and management access.
marketingHeadline: Firewall Configuration Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A firewall is only as good as its configuration - and many small business firewalls have wide-open rules, unsecured remote access, flat networks, and default admin settings. The Firewall Configuration Review examines your firewall's actual configuration: rules, remote access, segmentation, and management access. We identify open ports that shouldn't be open, remote access that bypasses security, lack of segmentation, and weak management access. You get a documented review of your firewall's security with specific changes to make. It's the review that finds the rules that shouldn't be there.
bestFor: Businesses with firewalls configured by a previous provider or done on the fly
Organizations concerned about open ports and remote access
Companies with flat networks and no segmentation
Businesses preparing for security or compliance reviews

Firewall configuration report with recommended changes

summary: Review options for backup internet, failover, and continuity.
marketingHeadline: ISP Failover Readiness Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When your internet goes down, your business stops - and most small businesses have no plan for how they'd stay online. The ISP Failover Readiness Review examines your options for backup internet, failover, and continuity. We review your current internet setup, assess whether backup connectivity is feasible in your location, and evaluate options like a second ISP, LTE or 5G backup, and automatic failover. You get a realistic assessment of your options with cost and reliability considerations - so when the primary connection fails, your business has a plan instead of a shutdown.

name: VLAN Setup
summary: Segment staff, guest, IoT, camera, or other device networks.
marketingHeadline: VLAN Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When staff computers, guest Wi-Fi, cameras, IoT devices, and phones all share one network, a compromise of any one device can reach everything. The VLAN Setup segments your network so different device types and user groups are isolated from each other. We plan and configure VLANs for staff, guest, IoT, cameras, and other device categories, set up the routing and security policies between them, and verify devices land in the right segments. Your network goes from flat and exposed to segmented and controlled - the way modern business networks are supposed to be.
bestFor: Businesses with cameras, IoT devices, and staff on one flat network
Organizations that want to limit the blast radius of a compromise
Companies with managed switches capable of VLANs but not using them
Businesses preparing for security or compliance reviews
whatIsIncluded: VLAN design for staff, guest, IoT, camera, and other segments
Routing and inter-segment security policy setup
customerOutcomes: A segmented network where devices are isolated by type
Reduced blast radius if any single device is compromised
Cameras, guests, IoT, and staff on controlled segments
A network designed the way business networks should be
whatIsNotIncluded: Hardware, licenses, subscriptions, permits, or third-party service fees unless explicitly included

name: Firewall Setup
summary: Deploy and configure a business firewall.
marketingHeadline: Firewall Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A business firewall is the gatekeeper of your network - controlling what comes in, what goes out, and who can manage your systems remotely. The Firewall Setup deploys and configures a business firewall properly for your environment. We install a suitable firewall, build a security rule set that allows what's needed and blocks what isn't, configure remote access securely, set up segmentation where appropriate, and document the whole configuration. Your network gets a real security boundary instead of whatever the router defaults were - with rules that protect rather than just pass traffic.
bestFor: Businesses with no dedicated firewall or only consumer router protections
Organizations that want a proper security boundary for their network
Companies that need secure remote access configured correctly
Businesses preparing for security or compliance reviews
whatIsIncluded: Security rule set design and configuration
customerOutcomes: A properly deployed business firewall
A security rule set that blocks what should be blocked
Secure remote access without wide-open exposure

name: Switch Installation
summary: Install or configure a managed network switch.
marketingHeadline: Switch Installation from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Managed switches are the backbone of a business network - handling wired connectivity, VLANs, and traffic management - but only if they're installed and configured properly. The Switch Installation service installs or configures a managed network switch the right way: physical installation, VLAN and port configuration, link testing, and integration with your network. We ensure wired devices connect reliably, ports are configured correctly, and the switch is set up for management rather than left as an expensive unconfigured hub. Your wired network gets the reliability and structure it needs.

summary: Document UniFi devices, ports, photos, IPs, controller notes, and topology.
marketingHeadline: UniFi Site Documentation from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: UniFi site documentation is the difference between a network you can manage and one you can only guess about. The UniFi Site Documentation documents your UniFi environment completely: devices, ports, photos, IPs, controller notes, and topology. We capture what's installed, how it's connected, how it's configured, and where it lives, producing documentation that makes management and troubleshooting straightforward. When something breaks or a new technician needs to understand your setup, the documentation is there. It's the kind of network knowledge most businesses only realize they lacked after an outage.

summary: Review recording, blind spots, storage, account access, and camera health.
marketingHeadline: Camera Health Check from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Camera systems fail silently - a camera stops recording, a blind spot develops, storage fills up, or an account becomes stale - and most businesses never notice until they need footage and find nothing there. The Camera Health Check reviews your camera system's health: recording status, blind spots, storage, account access, and camera condition. We verify cameras are actually recording, identify coverage gaps, check storage capacity and retention, review who has access, and assess camera health. You get a clear picture of your camera system's reliability before you need footage it didn't capture.
