name: Backup Readiness Check
summary: Determine whether critical business data is backed up and recoverable.
marketingHeadline: Backup Readiness Check from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Most small businesses believe their data is backed up - until a computer dies, a ransomware attack hits, or an employee deletes the wrong folder and the 'backup' turns out to be nothing. The Backup Readiness Check determines whether your critical business data is actually backed up and recoverable. We identify what data matters, verify what backup solutions exist (or don't), check whether they're configured and running, and test whether a restore would actually work. You get a clear, honest answer about your backup posture - and what it would take to be protected.
bestFor: Businesses that assume their data is backed up but haven't verified it
Organizations with no backup solution at all
Companies whose backups have never been tested
Businesses preparing for insurance that requires backup evidence
customerOutcomes: An honest answer about whether your data is really backed up
Critical data identified and its protection status documented
Backup gaps found before you need the backup
A clear path to actual data protection

marketingHeadline: Computer Backup Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A single workstation can hold months of irreplaceable business work - proposals, quotes, customer files, financials - and most businesses have no backup for it beyond 'I think it's in the cloud.' We identify the important data on the computer, set up automated backup to a reliable destination, configure retention, and verify a restore works. That one computer's data goes from at risk to protected - automatically, without relying on the user to remember anything.

name: Microsoft 365 Backup Setup
summary: Configure backup or retention strategy for Microsoft 365 data.
marketingHeadline: Microsoft 365 Backup Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Microsoft 365 gives you retention and recycling bins - not backup. If an employee permanently deletes mail, ransomware encrypts OneDrive files, or an insider wipes a SharePoint site, Microsoft won't restore it. The Microsoft 365 Backup Setup configures a proper backup solution for Exchange Online, SharePoint, and OneDrive with real point-in-time recovery. We select an appropriate backup platform, automate backup of your mailboxes, sites, and files, set sensible retention, and test a restore so you know it works. Your Microsoft 365 data finally gets the protection you've been assuming it has.

Companies that need mail, files, and sites recoverable beyond Microsoft's retention

summary: Perform or guide a controlled restore test and document results.

name: Business Continuity Starter Plan
summary: Identify critical systems, recovery targets, and business continuity contacts.
marketingHeadline: Business Continuity Starter Plan from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Business continuity is about keeping your business running when something goes wrong - which requires knowing what's truly critical and what you'd do to stay operational. The Business Continuity Starter Plan identifies your critical systems, recovery targets, and continuity contacts. We work through which systems must stay up, how fast each needs to recover, and who the key contacts are for people, vendors, and recovery. You get a plain-English continuity starting point that turns 'we'd figure it out' into a documented plan for staying in business during disruption.

name: Internet Failover Setup
summary: Configure backup internet or failover where available.
marketingHeadline: Internet Failover Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When your internet connection fails, your phones, payments, email, and customer access can all stop at once - and without backup connectivity, you're down until the ISP recovers. The Internet Failover Setup configures backup internet or failover where it's available. We assess your options, set up backup connectivity, configure automatic or manual failover, and test that it works. Your business gains the ability to stay online through an ISP outage - with failover that's configured and proven, not just an unused LTE device on a shelf.

name: Website Security Review
summary: Review SSL, admin access, plugins/dependencies, backups, and security posture.
marketingHeadline: Website Security Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: A compromised website can infect visitors, damage your reputation, and take your site offline - and most business sites have vulnerabilities nobody has checked. The Website Security Review examines your website's security posture: SSL, admin access, plugins and dependencies, backups, and overall risk. We check your SSL configuration, review admin accounts and access, identify outdated plugins or dependencies, verify backups, and assess common website vulnerabilities. You get a security assessment of your website with prioritized fixes - before a compromise happens, not after.
bestFor: Businesses worried about website compromise or defacement
Organizations running sites with outdated plugins or dependencies
Companies that want website security reviewed before it's a problem
Businesses preparing for insurance or compliance that covers web presence

name: Website Backup Setup
summary: Configure or guide website backup process.
marketingHeadline: Website Backup Setup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When a website gets hacked, a plugin update breaks the site, or someone deletes the wrong content, the fix depends on one thing: a backup you can restore. Most small business websites have no backup at all. The Website Backup Setup configures or guides a website backup process that protects your site and its content. We set up automated backups of your website files and database, configure retention, verify a restore works, and document the process. Your website data becomes recoverable - instead of being one mistake or attack away from disaster.

marketingHeadline: DNS Cleanup from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: DNS records accumulate over time - old hosting records, abandoned subdomains, forgotten services - and stale records create confusion, security risks, and deliverability problems. The DNS Cleanup removes stale DNS records and documents the important ones. We review your DNS zone, identify outdated and risky records, remove what you approve, and document what remains and why it matters. Your DNS goes from a messy collection of old records to a clean, documented, understood configuration - reducing risk and making changes straightforward.
bestFor: Businesses with DNS records accumulated over years
Organizations unsure what DNS records exist and why
Companies with abandoned subdomains or old hosting records
Businesses preparing for website, email, or provider changes
customerOutcomes: A clean, documented DNS configuration
Stale and risky records removed
Understanding of what each remaining record does
DNS that's safe and straightforward to manage

name: Email DNS Authentication Fix
summary: Review or configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC where possible.
marketingHeadline: Email DNS Authentication Fix from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Without proper SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records, your email domain can be spoofed, your mail lands in spam, and scammers can impersonate you to customers. The Email DNS Authentication Fix reviews or configures SPF, DKIM, and DMARC where possible. We assess your current email authentication, configure the records correctly (including the tricky SPF limit issue), and verify email deliverability and spoofing protection. You get email authentication that protects your domain from impersonation and improves deliverability - configured, tested, and documented.

Organizations concerned about domain spoofing

Businesses preparing for insurance that requires email authentication

marketingCopy: When an employee leaves, every account, key, and device they can access is a risk - and rushed offboarding leaves access that should have been removed. The Employee Offboarding Checklist creates an access removal and data preservation checklist for your business. We build a practical, role-aware checklist covering accounts to disable, access to revoke, devices to collect, data to preserve, and steps to complete before the employee's last day. You get a repeatable offboarding process that ensures no former employee retains access - and no important data is lost.

name: Quarterly Access Review
summary: Recurring user, admin, and vendor access review.
marketingHeadline: Quarterly Access Review from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: Access accumulates - employees change roles, vendors come and go, accounts are forgotten - and without regular review, access becomes outdated and risky. The Quarterly Access Review is a recurring review of user, admin, and vendor access. Each quarter we review who has access to what, identify stale and excessive access, and work with you to remove or correct what shouldn't be there. You get documented, recurring access review that keeps access aligned with reality - and provides the review evidence insurers and compliance frameworks increasingly require.
bestFor: Businesses that want access reviewed on a schedule
Organizations preparing for compliance that requires access reviews
Companies that want stale access removed regularly
Businesses that want documented access review evidence
customerOutcomes: Access reviewed and corrected quarterly
Stale and excessive access removed on schedule
Documented access review evidence
Access kept aligned with your business

Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for MCT Secure Care. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.

triage: Confirm purchase scope: "MCT Secure Care" for [customer]. Review managed it with deeper cybersecurity oversight. Verify customer expectations, timeline, and any prerequisites before scheduling.

Schedule session: coordinate with customer contact who has admin access and authority. Send calendar invite with preparation checklist: required credentials, system access, list of users/devices, any prior documentation.
Pre-work access check: verify customer has provided or confirmed admin access to required systems. If admin credentials are missing, request before proceeding — do not start without proper access.
Gather baseline: collect current documentation, previous IT provider notes, existing configurations, known issues, and any urgency or compliance factors. Note any deadlines or insurance requirements.

Create ticket: log in internal system with product ID "mct_secure_care", customer name, scope boundaries, expected deliverables, exclusions, and follow-up plan. Assign appropriate technician based on skill set.
delivery: Pre-work preparation: review customer intake responses, current documentation, and any previous service history. Prepare session with required tools: RMM dashboard, endpoint protection console, M365 Admin Center, backup monitoring, help desk ticketing. Confirm customer has provided required access.

Monthly execution: perform recurring tasks per plan scope — system monitoring review, patch status check, backup verification, help desk ticket resolution, security alert review.
Customer touchpoint: provide monthly summary of work performed, incidents resolved, and any recommendations. Schedule quarterly strategy review to discuss technology roadmap and improvements.

Technical verification: test all changes, configurations, or improvements made. For assessments: verify all findings are accurate and evidence-based. For setup/installation: verify all systems function correctly. For cleanup: verify no unintended removals occurred.

Prepare deliverables: compile all documentation, screenshots, configuration notes, and recommendations into a structured deliverable package. Format for customer readability — use plain English, highlight key findings, and prioritize recommendations.

Customer walkthrough: schedule 15-30 minute session to walk through findings/deliverables with the customer. Answer questions, provide context, and explain next steps. Get customer acknowledgment of service completion.
documentation: Record all findings, configurations, changes, and decisions made during the MCT Secure Care engagement. Use structured format: date, action, result, follow-up needed.
Create plain-English customer summary tailored to a non-technical audience. Explain what was done, what was found (if assessment), what was changed (if setup), and what it means for the business.
Include visual evidence: screenshots of configurations before and after, network diagrams or topology maps if applicable, benchmark results, coverage maps, or any other visual that adds clarity.

Document out-of-scope observations separately. If any issues were discovered outside the purchased scope, note them with a brief description and recommended follow-up action. Do not act on them without customer approval.

qa: Verify all work completed matches the purchased scope for MCT Secure Care. Check each bullet point in the service description — is it addressed? If not, note the reason.
Check that customer authorization was obtained for every change made. For any changes requiring explicit approval, verify the approval is documented (email, signed form, call log).
Secret audit: review all documentation, notes, and screenshots for stored credentials, API keys, recovery codes, or sensitive data. Remove or redact immediately if found.
Verify deliverable completeness: is the customer summary ready? Are all reports formatted correctly? Are screenshots included? Are recommendations prioritized?
Category-specific check: verify service-specific quality criteria are met.
Flag follow-up items: identify any recommended next steps, whether optional, recommended, or urgent. Tag items that should be addressed within 30 days vs longer-term.
closeout: Send final deliverables package to customer via email or secure portal. Include: customer summary, findings report (if applicable), configuration documentation (if applicable), and recommendations.
Attach or link all supporting materials: screenshots, diagrams, guides, policy documents, configuration exports. Ensure all links work and are accessible to the customer.
Recommend next-step services: based on findings and customer needs, suggest: related bundles, monthly plans, or category-specific follow-up services.
Revoke temporary access: if temporary admin access was granted for the engagement, confirm it has been revoked. If the customer provided credentials, remind them to rotate passwords if appropriate.

Record internal notes: add ticket notes with key technical details for future reference. Note any customer-specific configurations, access methods, or environmental details that will help on future engagements.

Schedule follow-up: if recommendations include specific actions, schedule a reminder to follow up in 30-60 days. For monthly plan customers, confirm next recurring engagement date. For bundles, confirm all components were delivered.

summary: Immediate containment guidance and triage for suspected ransomware or malware.
marketingHeadline: Ransomware First Response from Maine Cyber Tech
marketingCopy: When ransomware hits, every hour matters - systems encrypted, backups questioned, business operations at stake. MCT Ransomware First Response is an immediate incident response for ransomware: isolating systems, preserving evidence, and guiding recovery. When ransomware strikes, we act fast to contain the spread, preserve evidence for insurance and law enforcement, and coordinate your recovery path. This is the first-response service for a ransomware event - the immediate containment and guidance that limits damage.
